'''Hardley Flood''' is a {{convert|49.8  |ha|acre|abbr=off|adj=on}} biological [[Site of Special Scientific Interest]] near [[Loddon, Norfolk|Loddon]], between [[Norwich]], [[Lowestoft]] and [[Great Yarmouth]] in [[Norfolk|Norfolk, England]].<ref name=dsv>{{cite web|url=  https://designatedsites.naturalengland.org.uk/SiteDetail.aspx?SiteCode=S1000432&SiteName=&countyCode=29&responsiblePerson=&SeaArea=&IFCAArea= |title=Designated Sites View: Hardley Flood | series= Sites of Special Scientific Interest|publisher=Natural England|access-date = 12 June 2018}}</ref><ref name=map>{{cite web|url= http://magic.defra.gov.uk/MagicMap.aspx?startTopic=Designations&activelayer=sssiIndex&query=HYPERLINK%3D%271000432%27|title=Map of Hardley Flood|series= Sites of Special Scientific Interest|publisher=Natural England|access-date= 12 June 2018}}</ref> It is part of the Broadland [[Ramsar site]]<ref name=broadram>{{cite web|url=  https://designatedsites.naturalengland.org.uk/SiteGeneralDetail.aspx?SiteCode=UK11010&SiteName=&countyCode=29&responsiblePerson=&unitId=&SeaArea=&IFCAArea= |title=Designated Sites View: Broadland | series= Ramsar Sites|publisher=Natural England|access-date = 25 May 2018}}</ref> and [[Special Protection Area]],<ref name=broadspa>{{cite web|url=  https://designatedsites.naturalengland.org.uk/SiteGeneralDetail.aspx?SiteCode=UK9009253&SiteName=&countyCode=29&responsiblePerson=&unitId=&SeaArea=&IFCAArea= |title=Designated Sites View: Broadland | series= Special Protection Areas|publisher=Natural England|access-date = 25 May 2018}}</ref> and The Broads [[Special Area of Conservation]].<ref name=broadssac>{{cite web|url= https://designatedsites.naturalengland.org.uk/SiteGeneralDetail.aspx?SiteCode=UK0013577&SiteName=&countyCode=29&responsiblePerson=&unitId=&SeaArea=&IFCAArea=  |title=Designated Sites View: The Broads | series= Special Areas of Conservation|publisher=Natural England|access-date = 25 May 2018}}</ref>

This area of tidal lagoons and reedbeds provides a [[spillway]] for the [[River Chet]]. The reedbeds provide nesting sites for birds, including nationally important populations of several breeding birds. Three rare flies have been recorded, ''[[Elachiptera uniseta]]'', ''[[Elachiptera scrobiculata]]'' and ''[[Lonchoptera scutellata]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://designatedsites.naturalengland.org.uk/PDFsForWeb/Citation/1000432.pdf   |title=Hardley Flood citation|series= Sites of Special Scientific Interest|publisher=Natural England|access-date=12   June 2018}}</ref>

The site is open to  the public.
